NINE DECLARED DIVERGENCES, AND A RULE THAT SAYS WHAT IT ENFORCES.
This read FOUR DECLARED DIVERGENCES and `a finding outside this list is a defect`. On the run
it was written against, 97 findings were described as all falling inside those four, and 49 of
them did not: twelve on the router-stopped state — ten of those citing spec-M15 §2's seventh
assumption by name — one on M18's `Choose…`, and thirty-six on three classes the list had no
number for at all. Only two of the four carried a finding; the other two carried none, and
nobody had added the ledger's own rows up. An allowance list that does not adjudicate its own
findings is worse than no list, because the next reader learns it is not authoritative — the
same lesson a scanned-file count teaches when it can fall by ten without anything going red.
So the list below is complete, every row of settings.pairing.tsv carries the number of the
divergence its finding falls under, and the rule is:
EVERY CITATION OPENS WITH `Dn · `. A finding whose citation carries no number, or a number
this list does not define, is a defect. Nothing here has to be taken on trust: the numbers
are in the citation column of the generated ledger, so the split is re-measurable in three
lines against the run that wrote it rather than against this file.
F='| \(absent\|divergent\|extra\|extra-cited\|unclassified\) |'
grep -c "$F" planning/fidelity/settings.ledger.md            # findings
grep "$F" planning/fidelity/settings.ledger.md | grep -c '| D[0-9] ·'   # adjudicated
grep -o '| D[0-9] ·' planning/fidelity/settings.ledger.md | sort | uniq -c  # the split
The first two numbers must be equal and the third must sum to them. `structure-unpaired`,
`present` and `covered-by-pair` are excluded because none of the three appends a finding.
WHAT IS NOT ENFORCED, stated rather than implied: no layer FAILS on an untagged citation.
The engine reads column four of the pairing as free text, and teaching it this rule is an
edit to scripts/acceptance/mock_fidelity.py, which is outside the item that wrote this note.
The tag makes the adjudication derivable from the run's own artifact; it does not make it
automatic, and a reader who wants the guarantee should run the three lines above.
The counts are this run's, and they are the ledger's, not this file's arithmetic.
1. THE SOURCE LIST IS 256pt AND THE MOCK DRAWS 200. Owner: M21. 0 findings. Not "we could
not derive 200". A settings source list is a sidebar, DESIGN.md §2 specifies `Sidebar
256pt`, MetricToken.sidebar is that value, and the mock's own mac-craft:metrics block
carries `sidebar 256px` and no 200 of any name — so the mock disagrees with itself as well
as with the document. DesignTokenParityTests compares MetricToken's name set against §2's
table for exact equality in both directions, so a `settingsSidebar` case without a new §2
row reddens it, and authoring that row is M21's substance. It carries no finding because
the geometry layer compares PAIRED nodes and the source list is unpaired for D7's reason:
the mock draws it outside every `.v-*` frame, so there is no mock geometry to compare to.
2. FOUR OF THE SEVEN SOURCE-LIST SYMBOLS HAVE NO Icon CASE. Owner: M21. 0 findings, for the
same reason as 1 — the symbols are inside the nav the census cannot reach. The mock draws
#i-servers, #i-harness, #i-bolt, #i-download, #i-shield, #i-menubar and #i-sliders; Icon
carries servers, bolt and shield exactly and has no harness, download, menubar or sliders.
Its count is asserted as spriteSymbols (21) + drawnReplacementsForUnicode (1) against THE
PROTOTYPE's sprite in DesignSystemTests, so adding four cases re-bases that inventory from
one document to the other. The panes reuse layers, tray, list and settings instead.
3. THE MOCK IS A TAB SET AND THE BUILD IS A SPLIT VIEW. Owner: nobody — it is the conversion.
14 findings. All seven panes sit in the mock's DOM at once with `.active` deciding which is
visible, so `v-ideal` inventories all seven panes' contents; a NavigationSplitView detail
renders the selected pane and nothing else. Six of the seven panes are therefore absent
from any one run. This is a difference in how the surface is modelled, not a missing
control, and closing it would mean rendering seven panes at once.
4. AFFORDANCES NAMING CAPABILITIES THIS PRODUCT DOES NOT HAVE. Owner: whichever item builds
the capability; the row becomes buildable then and not before. 34 findings.
TWENTY-TWO OF THE MOCK'S THIRTY ROWS are not built — the thirty are the `.form-row`
elements of `v-ideal` at design/mcp-router-console.html:1554-1711, and the eight that ARE
built are Endpoint, Idle window, Warm set, Control token, Paired devices, Show in the menu
bar, Router log and Configuration. Three of those eight are drawn as observed facts with the
mock's own control left off, which is why 34 affordances rather than 22 land here: a row can
carry a popup and its chevron, and `5 minutes`, `Rotate…` and both `Reveal in Finder`
buttons are absent from rows that are otherwise built. `Start the router` in `v-empty` is
the thirty-fifth mock affordance of this class and the one outside the thirty. spec-M15 §2's
fifth assumption forbids building a control for a capability the product does not have, and
every such row carries the pre-existing artifact that recorded the absence in
settings.pairing.tsv.
THIS COUNT READ THIRTEEN in four places until M15's gap-fix counted the mock directly.
Nothing derived it: the ledger's own rows were never added up, and the honesty test that
enforces the rule listed sixteen labels covering fifteen of the twenty-two, so the sentence
and the rule under it disagreed by seven rows and neither could see the other.
5. THE ROUTER IS STOPPED: THE MOCK REFUSES THE WINDOW AND THE BUILD KEEPS IT LIVE. Owner:
nobody — it is spec-M15 §2's SEVENTH assumption, "With the router stopped the window still
opens and says so, rather than refusing to open", taken deliberately against the mock.
12 findings. The mock's `v-empty` frame replaces the whole window with an icon, a headline
and a `Start the router` button; the build keeps the window, the source list, the pane hero
and both groups live — because MenuBarPane reads nothing from the router and stays editable
— and renders ControlAPIError's own headline and advice in place of the router facts. So
every live node reads `extra` and the mock's three refusal affordances read `absent`. The
offline banner carrying no action button is spec-M8's recorded DESIGN.md §5 deviation and
is inside this divergence rather than beside it.
6. A SHEET OPENED FROM A PANE IS M18's. Owner: M18. 1 finding — the Warm set row's `Choose…`,
which opens the warm-set editor. planning/features-to-triage/M18-sheets-and-gates.md owns
every sheet a pane would open, and §4 leaves no pane in this build opening one, which is
also why requirement 11 could not be tested here.
7. THE MOCK'S AFFORDANCE CENSUS DOES NOT REACH THE STRUCTURE THE BUILD DRAWS. Owner: nobody —
it is mock-affordances.py's rule set against the mock's own markup, and it is an instrument
limit rather than a product difference. 28 findings, the largest class after D4. Three
shapes, all of them the same mechanism: the pane list is a <nav class="swin-side"> INSIDE
.swin-split and OUTSIDE every .v-* frame, so no state census can reach it (16); the mock's
.form-group and .form-row match none of the declared affordance kinds at
mock-affordances.py:29-50, so the card and rows the build draws its values in have nothing
on the mock side to pair with (9); and the mock's own helper prose is a <span> inside .fl,
which no rule matches either (3). Closing any of the three means changing what the census
inventories, which re-bases every surface's breadth layer at once.
8. M8's SHIPPED SETTINGS SURFACE, CARRIED FORWARD, THAT THE MOCK DOES NOT DRAW. Owner: M8 —
spec-M15's own requirement is that nothing a person can set today stops being settable.
7 findings: the four named group headers Router / Menu bar / Warm set / Control token,
which scripts/acceptance/m8-settings-menubar.sh reads back off the rendered window while
the mock draws one unlabelled .form-group per pane (5), and `Show in Servers`, which is M8's
shipped action pointing at the switch on each server's own row where the mock offers a
sheet (2). These are real product differences with an owner, which is what separates them
from D7.
9. THE MOCK STATES FIGURES NOTHING IN THIS PROCESS OBSERVES. Owner: nobody — DESIGN.md §6.
1 finding: the footer callout `MCP Router 1.4.0 (build 2026.08.19) · Developer ID signed
and notarised`. Every build in this repository is unsigned (Makefile:11-22), so the second
clause is two facts nothing measures, and BuildIdentity draws a version only when the
bundle carries one. It would remain a finding with all seven panes rendered — the strings
would differ rather than the affordance being absent — which is why it is not D3's.
`loading` and `error` are OMITTED FROM states AND INVENTORIED HERE rather than dropped in
silence, which is M23's A6 precedent. spec-M15 §2's ninth assumption gives the panes' loading
and error wording to M17; listing them here without building them would make every run exit 1
on absent affordances, which reports a scope boundary as a defect. Owner: M17.
THE FLOORS ARE RECORDED, NOT CHOSEN, and that is the mechanism rather than a hole in it. They
are the census sizes measured on the first run whose structure layer was clean, they only ever
rise, and Context.__init__ exits 3 for a floor below 1 or non-integer. A floor lowered later to
make a run green is the failure this shape has to be watched for: a shrunken denominator raises
reported coverage while measuring less, which planning/evidence/P4-acceptance.md records four
separate times.
`lintFiles` was written 126 and corrected to 125 INSIDE this item, and the correction is
recorded rather than quietly applied because it is the shape the paragraph above warns about.
The first structurally-clean run happened before the run that measured two Settings items in
the app menu; removing the duplicate deleted SettingsCommandItem.swift, and the lint's scan
count genuinely fell by one. The ratchet against main is intact either way: main scans 118.

layers.name: font-weight-face
layers.substitute: A SwiftUI Font is opaque — String(describing: Font.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)) returns "Font(provider: SwiftUI.FontBox<SwiftUI.Font.SystemProvider>)", with no size, weight or face in it. Confirmed instead by: the TypeToken each text node names is recorded in tokens["type"] at apply time and checked against the measured line box by the type-metrics layer; DesignTokenParityTests pins the eight-role ladder against DESIGN.md; scripts/lint/no-raw-design-values.sh fails any font size that does not come off it. None of the three can see an ancestor .font() winning the cascade, and that residue is what this row is.
